[architecture] Sequence 6 (Membrane) temperature/humidity hold points (28°C, 80%) lack BOM forecast source or real-time monitoring assignment.

[hrcw] Task 5 (Investigate slab): HRCW false but dominant hazard is dust inhalation—silica dust control adequate but HRCW logic inconsistent with height exposure during balcony work.

[hrcw] Task 4 (Remove waterproofing): HRCW false, dominant hazard is silica dust. Silica controls present (wet method, HEPA, P2 RPE, sample hold) but asbestos hold-point wording weak: 'assume potential hazard unless certified otherwise' is not a prohibition.

[hrcw] Task 6 (Apply membrane): Dominant hazard VOC inhalation, controls adequate. Temperature/humidity limits (28°C, 80% RH) reasonable but no reference to product flash point or fire hazard if solvents used.

[hrcw] Task 9 (Final inspection): HRCW true (cl.2 fall >2m) but hazards list includes trip hazard, dust, slip—none directly support HRCW selection. Dominant hazard 'fall from height during close inspection' is accurate but low-consequence inspection task; severity appears overcalled vs. actual scope.
[hrcw] Task 11 (Dismantle scaffold): HRCW true, dominant hazard fall from height >4m—appropriate. Controls and stop-work triggers comprehensive.
[hrcw] Task 8 (Reinstate balustrades): HRCW true (cl.2 fall >2m), dominant hazard fall from unguarded edge, controls include temporary edge protection, harness, hoist—appropriate match.
[hrcw] Task 2 (Erect scaffold): HRCW true (cl.2 fall >2m), hazards and controls well-matched. Base plate security and torque wrench monitoring explicit.
[hrcw] Task 1 (Establish site): HRCW false, dominant hazard vehicle strike in occupied courtyard—appropriate. No overcall; controls focus on exclusion zones and spotters.
[hrcw] Task 3 (Isolate spaces): HRCW true (cl.2 WAH-H6) but scope is internal netting/barriers, not fall-risk activity. HRCW selection appears overcalled; hazard is barrier collapse, not worker fall.

[hrcw] Task 7 (Reinstate screed/tile): HRCW false, dominant hazard manual handling and slip—appropriate for low-risk tiling task. No height exposure noted; controls omit dust extraction if grinding is part of rework.

[hrcw] Task 10 (Reinstate spaces): HRCW false, dominant hazard dust release during barrier removal—appropriate. Controls wet-down method adequate; no dust extraction specified but scope is removal/cleanup, not generation.
[hrcw] Task 12 (Demobilise): HRCW false, dominant hazard vehicle strike—appropriate. Vehicle movement plan, spotters, barricading specified; load stability check added.

[hrcw] Silica adequacy: Tasks 4 and 5 include wet cleaning, HEPA extraction, P2/P3 RPE, and sample retention. Asbestos: Task 4 requires sample hold if pre-1990, but wording 'assume potential hazard unless certified otherwise' is conditional, not mandatory prohibition.
[hrcw] Hazmat: Task 6 (membrane) requires SDS review and VOC controls; Task 7 (grout/adhesive) references SDS but no explicit ventilation adequacy check for occupied space.
[hrcw] CCVS code alignment: Tasks using SIL-H6 (silica) in Tasks 4, 5, 7 and CHM-H6 (chemical) in Task 6 appear correct. Task 3 assigned WAH-H6 despite non-fall scope.
[hrcw] Undercall risk: Task 7 (screed/tile) mentions grout fumes in adjacent spaces but no respiratory protection specified for indoor grouting; may undercall if solvent-based adhesive used.

[hrcw] Overcall risk: Task 3 (isolate spaces) marked HRCW cl.2 but worker hazard is barrier collapse, not fall from height. Task 9 (final inspection) marked HRCW but scope is inspection walk, not structural work; trip/fall consequence is low.

[hrcw] Hold-point logic: Task 4 asbestos hold weak ('assume...unless certified') vs. Task 3 (requires 'written notification'). Task 5 requires Leo & Associates sign-off before membrane—appropriate gating.
[hrcw] Documentation gap: Task 6 membrane application omits flash point or fire hazard despite solvent use; Task 7 no explicit ventilation adequacy check for occupied-building grout fumes.
[ccvs] Task 5 (Investigate slab substrate): CCVS code SYS-M3 misaligned. Dominant hazard is dust inhalation (silica) — should map to SIL-H6, not SYS-M3 (systems/admin control).

[ccvs] Task 4 (Remove waterproofing): CCVS code SIL-H6 correct for silica hazard, but monitoring critical_control describes dust extraction — contradicts dominant_hazard focusing on silica. Evidence field weak: no respirator cartridge change logs specified.

[ccvs] Task 6 (Apply membrane): CCVS code CHM-H6 correct for chemical/VOC hazard. Monitoring evidence field incomplete — no specific vapour concentration threshold or headache log requirement documented.

[ccvs] Task 3 (Isolate spaces): CCVS code WAH-H6 applied but dominant hazard is barrier collapse (structural), not working at height. Should be SYS-H6 or structural control code. WAH dominance questionable.

[ccvs] Task 7 (Reinstate screed): CCVS code SIL-H6 but dominant hazard is manual handling (low-back strain from troweling), not silica. Should map to manual handling/ergonomic control code. Misalignment.

[ccvs] Task 9 (Final inspection): CCVS code SYS-M3 assigned but task is primarily fall-at-height risk (>2m balcony edge inspection). Should be WAH-H6. Responsibility field generic and does not match task scope.

[ccvs] Task 12 (Demobilise): CCVS code SYS-M3 assigned but dominant hazard is vehicle strike in occupied courtyard — should map to vehicle/traffic control code (VEH-H6 or equivalent). WAH not applicable but monitoring section shows generic exclusion zone language.

[ccvs] Task 7 (Screed): Monitoring critical_control field copy-pasted from Task 5 (dust extraction / grinding) — operationally incorrect for tiling/screed. Does not reflect actual control (manual handling rotation, hydration, slip prevention).
[ccvs] Task 9 (Inspection) & Task 11 (Dismantle): Responsibility field identical (scaffolder-centric fall harness language) despite different scopes (inspection vs. dismantling). Copy-paste defect.
[ccvs] Task 10 (Reinstate spaces): Evidence field references 'dust extraction running' but task scope is barrier removal and cleaning, not dust-generating work. Monitoring misaligned with hazard.

[ccvs] WAH applicability: Tasks 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, 11 marked WAH-applicable = TRUE, but Tasks 3 & 9 dominant hazards do not clearly require fall protection (barrier collapse, inspection slip). Over-classification creates hold-point bloat.

[ccvs] Missing CCVS rows: No tasks assigned to vehicle/traffic control (VEH), manual handling (MH), or ergonomic (ERG) codes despite multiple hazards. Remedial scope implies high manual/handling exposure.
[ccvs] N/A hazard masking: Task 1 & 12 list 'Vehicle strike' as dominant but no dedicated vehicle control CCVS code used. Risk treated as WAH/SYS fallback.

[credibility] Task 4 (Remove waterproofing): Latent asbestos presumption embedded as live scope control—source says 'hold samples...if building predates 1990' but live tasks list 'assume potential hazard unless certified'. Asbestos testing is gating control, not live work package task.

[credibility] Task 5 (Investigate slab): CCVS code SYS-M3 (systems/materials) assigned but dominant hazard and controls are dust suppression during concrete grinding—should be WAH-H6 or SIL-H6 to reflect actual work type and hazard family.

[credibility] Task 4 dominant hazard mismatch: listed as 'silica dust' but scope says 'latent asbestos condition'—hazard hierarchy incoherent; HOLD point correctly gates work but live controls conflate two different exposure risks.
[credibility] Task 9 (Final inspection): CCVS code SYS-M3 assigned but task is balcony edge inspection at height >2m—should be WAH-H6 to match HRCW true and dominant hazard 'fall from height'.

[credibility] Task 7 (Reinstate screed) monitoring section references 'dust extraction' and 'P2 respirator' but those controls are not listed in live task controls—monitoring evidence misaligned with stated controls.

[credibility] Task 3 (Isolate spaces): CCVS code WAH-H6 assigned but task is temporary barrier installation in occupied building interior—dominant hazard is barrier collapse, not working at height; HRCW=true appears unsupported.
